findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike reported a campaign against South Korean financial organizations active from late September to early October 2026 that resulted in data exfiltration. Investigators found ARTEX configuration files and Claude Code session histories on attacker-controlled infrastructure; the ARTEX instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash, with GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 used in additional Claude Code sessions. The actor was not attributed to a named adversary and was assessed with moderate confidence to be a financially motivated Chinese speaker.

findings.title: Chinese developer makes Artex AI agent closed-source after South Korean bank hack
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported that Autumn-27 announced on October 8 that ARTEX would become closed source, with no further public versions or maintenance. The developer said the tool was intended for security testing and bore no responsibility for illegal misuse; the GitHub page was subsequently taken down. The report said at least nine South Korean banks had disclosed targeting or been identified as targets in local reporting.

findings.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
findings.summary_md: Microsoft attributed the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise to Storm-0940, a China-state-aligned actor using ARTEX against hundreds of organizations globally as early as September 2026. It reported attempts to sign in to more than 2,250 tenants and multiple cases where initial targeting led to privileged cloud access in less than three hours. A password-spray subset from October 10 to 14 generated more than 151,000 failed logons and peaked at 2,900 failures per minute on October 11, with no successful authentication observed in that subset.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys observed 1,465 hosts exposing an ARTEX console as of November 4, 2026, while cautioning that some belonged to authorized testers. Two identically configured hosting blocks accounted for about 650 hosts, leaving roughly 815 distinct-looking deployments. It also found open directories on 32 ARTEX hosts exposing post-exploitation tools and identified default console port 8787, with 8790 and 443 also common.

findings.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
findings.summary_md: Microsoft documented threat actors using ARTEX to search public GitHub repositories for credentials, application secrets and AI-service API keys, then abuse them for cloud access. In one observed chain, an agent moved from GitHub secret discovery to Azure Key Vault data exfiltration in five minutes. The company supplied Entra service-principal and Graph hunting queries, containment guidance and indicators tied to the observed application-credential abuse.

findings.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
findings.summary_md: Microsoft reported that Cambodia-based Storm-3358 began using ARTEX against financial organizations in October 2026. The cluster combined the framework with internet scanning, exploitation of anonymous file upload and SSRF flaws, and installation of WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2 for persistence and lateral movement. The advisory included endpoint hunting guidance and indicators for ARTEX servers and command-and-control infrastructure active as of November 6.

findings.title: The ARTEX framework
findings.summary_md: F5 Labs documented ARTEX's release on July 26, 2026 and removal on October 8 after reports of malicious misuse. It reported more than 1,000 surviving GitHub repositories and over 1,600 publicly exposed consoles observed in November. The analysis describes adaptive WAF probing, custom web shells and RAT deployment, and recommends behavioral detection, API defenses, segmentation and least privilege rather than static signatures alone.
